p: The video opens with hook text questioning which Slack document version is latest, then demos a workflow where a user comments on a shared document, triggers an AI agent via terminal, and sees the doc update in real time at the same URL before ending on a CTA screen.
Artifact Share lets teams collaborate on a single document URL where human comments prompt AI agents to directly update the content.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Hook text displayed addressing document version confusion in Slack."},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"User highlights document title and submits a comment modal."},{"timestamp":"00:15","observation":"Terminal executes Claude command to ingest comment and republish."},{"timestamp":"00:20","observation":"Document updates smoothly in place while preserving the URL."},{"timestamp":"00:26","observation":"Ending slide displays tagline and artifactshare.com link."}]

The video clearly communicates the core value proposition and follows a logical workflow demonstration. Text and UI elements remain legible throughout. However, pacing drags slightly in the middle, and the overall duration significantly exceeds a typical five-second format.

p: ["opens on a dense wall of body text instead of a scroll-stopping hook","planned 'Slack, 10 versions, which is latest' hook never appears — creative diverges from brief","no explicit Artifact Share logo/wordmark or CTA overlay in any frame","terminal pane dominates screen real estate, pulling focus from the product UI"]

The demoed loop (comment on the doc → agent edits via CLI → same URL updates, confirmed by the resolved-comment panel) is a clean, legible proof of the core message 'humans point, agents edit,' and the closing caption states it plainly. But the actual footage abandons the stated hook concept entirely — there's no Slack, no messy version pile, so the intended pattern-interrupt never happens; instead viewers get a paragraph of dense text and a terminal window, which is a slow, low-tension open for a scroll-stopping ad. No visible product name/logo or explicit CTA text means salience and click-intent lean on the viewer inferring the takeaway themselves.
